Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Goid Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG OPINION NO. 25 S. 08 March 2010 MAYOR BENJAMIN C. ABALOS, JR. Mandaluyong City ATTN. Catherine Jane DL. Arce Chief, BPLO Dear Mayor Abalos: Greetings! 2010 Last year, we received a letter, with attachments, from the Lim and Leynes Law Offices in behalf of their client, Dolmar Property Ventures, Inc. (DPVI), requesting our legal opinion on the following matters, to wit. "1 ) Whether or not the tax assessment made by BPLO against the company is valid and proper (considering that business taxes based on income from the sale of Units in the Subdivisions are currently being paid by DPVI to the local government units where the Subdivisions are located); 2) Whether or not Section 150, Republic Act No. 7160 applies to real estate developers such as DPVI for purposes of determining liability for business taxes; and 3) Whether or not a Sanggunian Resolution specifically authorizing the City to tax real estate dealers such as DPVI is required before DPVI may be assessed business taxes, in accordance with Section 143 (h), Republic Act 7160." Much as we would like to immediately give due course to the subject letter of the Lim and Leynes Law Offices, we are apprehensive that we cannot properly act on it without referring the matter to you for your initial comment and/or clarification. We noticed that in the subject letter by the Lim and Leynes Law Offices, it was represented in Paragraph 6 therein that the controversy, from which the above-enumerated queries arose, began when the Mandaluyong City classified DPVI as a 'financial and investment company," deviating from its original classification as a "real estate dealer." However, a perusal of the letter dated 01 October 2009 of Ms. Catherine Jane DL. Arce to DPVI stated that the nature of business as a 'financial and investment company" was nonetheless applied for by the DPVI.

-2- Furthermore, it was also stated in the letter of the Lim and Leynes Law Offices that, despite DPVl's change or deviation of classification of the nature of its business, the Mandaluyong City still assessed DPVI with business taxes in the same manner as it was assessed in its original categorization. On the other hand, in the aforesaid letter of Ms. Arce to DPVI, it was stated that the latter under declared its gross receipts for the period from 2004 to 2006 In view of the foregoing rather inconsistent representations to this Department, we are referring the attached letter of the Lim and Leynes Law Offces to you for your initial comment and/or clarification. We will appreciate if we receive your comment and/or clarification the soonest possible time so that we will be guided on our course of action. Thank you and warm regards. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE O Undersecretary Legal/ 17
